messages.author: 06ad081d889cd1e0
messages.subject: Reactive graphs
parts:
Hi,
       Are the graphs reactive because we select parameters in the UI ? I would like to pull data using Java and push it to the R graphs  rendered by Shiny. RxJava can be reactive but I don't know if Java integration with R can update my graph shown by Shiny.

Any suggestions ?


Thanks,
Mohan

messages.author: 06ad081d889cd1e0
messages.subject: Re: Reactive graphs
parts:
I think I mean something like this. http://darrenjw.wordpress.com/2011/01/01/calling-java-code-from-r/

But reactive applications need not be called. So instead of R calling Java I would setup a notification mechanism and the new data from Java will somehow find its way to the R data structure. Am I dreaming here ?

Thanks,
Mohan

messages.author: 06ad081d889cd1e0
messages.subject: Re: Reactive graphs
parts:
Hi,
        Yes. The graphs show the current memory usage. So the graphs move and the window that is shown corresponds to the current time period which can be a minute or two. It is like the profilers that show usage.

The other type of graphs are static but the viewport should move left or right when it is dragged.
The data for all this is updated by a reactive java layer outside R using rJava.


Thanks,
Mohan
